evidence.summary: Learning objective and scope: Establishes that the screen is a `pygame.Surface`, that additional Surfaces can be created in memory, that `blit()` composes them, and covers colorkey vs per-pixel alpha transparency.

`pygame.Surface((100,100))` plus `screen.blit(sprajt, (50,50))` places the surface at exactly that point. -- Confirmed -- `screen.get_at((60,60))` returns Color(255,100,100,255) and get_at((10,10)) the background, reproducing the notebook transcript.

Per-pixel alpha requires the SRCALPHA flag; without it a fill's alpha component is ignored. -- Confirmed -- filling a plain Surface with (255,0,0,128) and blitting yields (255,0,0), while the same fill on `pygame.Surface(size, pygame.SRCALPHA)` yields (128,0,0).
`.convert()` discards per-pixel alpha; `.convert_alpha()` preserves it. -- Confirmed -- a pixel with alpha 100 becomes alpha 255 after .convert() and stays 100 after .convert_alpha().

Forgetting `screen.fill()` leaves trails; forgetting `display.flip()` leaves a black window. -- Confirmed -- the trail bug is genuinely reproduced in the shipped figure debug-missing-fill-trail.png, generated by really omitting the fill.
